source.notes: SPECIMEN Question Paper for the ICSE 2027 Examination, Chemistry (Science Paper – 2), printed 'T27 522 – SPECIMEN' on every page (used as paperCode). Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed Two hours (120 minutes). Section A (Question 1–2, 40 marks) is compulsory; Section B (Question 3–8, 40 marks) instructs 'Attempt any four questions' out of the six, each worth 10 marks — these are six independent, complete questions, NOT internal-choice OR pairs (the paper prints no 'OR' anywhere), so all six are included here without choiceGroup/part alternatives. Summing every printed mark in this pack therefore totals 100 (40 + 6×10), which is expected and not an error: a candidate only answers 4 of the 6 Section-B questions to reach the printed maximum of 80. The official marking scheme ('ICSE 2027 SPECIMEN DRAFT MARKING SCHEME – CHEMISTRY (SCIENCE PAPER 2)') is printed in the same PDF (pages 17–21) and is itself labelled 'DRAFT' by CISCE; answerSourceUrl is therefore the same URL as sourceUrl and answerSourceFile is null. Question 1's 15 MCQ sub-parts are each 1 mark (marking scheme marks them '[15x1]'); the printed [15] is the Question-1 total. Several multi-lettered sub-questions ((a)-(e) etc.) were split into separate entries worth 1 mark each when the marking scheme confirms an even per-item split (e.g. '[5x1]') or when each item is a self-contained equation/naming/observation prompt (in a few such splits a shared list instruction, e.g. 'Name the following:' or 'Identify the reactants P, Q and R in the following reactions:', was printed once for all items; this is noted per question). Where marks were only given as one combined total with no per-item confirmation in either the QP or the marking scheme, marksSource is set to SECTION_INSTRUCTIONS and the assumed even split is noted in that question's extractionIssues. Sub-questions built around a shared stem, diagram or dataset (e.g. Q2(i)'s electrolysis diagram, Q4(ii)'s pH 2/7/13 solutions, Q4(iii)'s iron-chloride sequence, Q5(iv)'s P/Q electron data, Q6(ii)'s decomposition data, Q6(iii)'s two test tubes, Q7(iv)'s esterification set-up, Q8(i)'s metal Z, Q8(iii)'s five organic structures) were kept together as one CASE_BASED/SHORT_ANSWER/NUMERICAL entry with the parts embedded in the text, per the brief, since the parts cannot stand alone without that shared context. Cognitive-level tags ('[Recall]'/'[Understanding]'/'[Application]'/'[Analysis]') are printed in the paper's right margin next to each sub-question, but the PDF text layer displaces them from their exact row (they surface a line or more away from their question, sometimes duplicated). Tags were attached to questions by matching the sequential top-to-bottom order in which the tags appear to the sequential top-to-bottom order of the sub-questions — verified for Question 1, where exactly 15 tags appear in the document for its 15 sub-parts — and cross-checked against the non -layout text extraction, where tags consistently trail immediately after each item's own text. Where a merged multi-part entry's sub-parts carry different tags, cognitiveLevel is omitted from that entry and the individual tag-to-part mapping is given in extractionIssues instead; where all of a merged entry's sub-parts share one tag, that single tag is used. Chemical formula subscripts/superscripts came out flat in the text layer throughout (e.g. H2SO4, C3H8O, Al3+, OH-1) and are kept as extracted; flagged per question where they appear in equations of two or more formulae. Diagrams, structural formulas and one data table are not reproduced; flagged per question with hasFigure and extractionIssues. Question 1(xiv) (four unlabelled reactions shown only in an unreproduced diagram) does not clearly fit any single listed chapter; 'acids-bases-and-salts' is recorded as the nearest genuinely-related guess (neutralisation producing water is the most common curriculum reaction of this kind), since check-sources.mjs requires a valid chapter slug for every question, but this particular mapping is low-confidence and should be checked by an editor.

questions.text:
20 grams of a gas M2P has lesser number of moles than 20 grams of the gas MP.
Justify the above statement using mathematical calculations.
[At.wt. M=14, P=16]
extractionIssues: Subscripts flattened: M2P.

officialAnswer.text:
44g of M2P = 1 Mole; 20 g of M2P = 1×20/44 = 0.44 moles.
30 g of MP = 1 mole; 20g of MP = 1×20/30 = 0.66 moles.
Therefore, M2P has a lesser number of moles.

questions.text:
Solid ammonium dichromate decomposes as under:
(NH4)2Cr2O7 → N2 + Cr2O3 + 4H2O
If 126 g of ammonium dichromate decomposes, calculate:
(a) the number of moles of ammonium dichromate that undergoes decomposition.
(b) the mass of chromic oxide formed at the same time.
(c) the volume of nitrogen gas evolved at STP.
[At wt: N = 14, Cr = 52, O = 16, H = 1]
extractionIssues: Subscripts flattened: (NH4)2Cr2O7, N2, Cr2O3, H2O.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) 252 g of Ammonium dichromate = 1 mole; 126 g of Ammonium dichromate = 0.5 moles
(b) 252 g of ammonium dichromate gives 152 g of chromic oxide; 126 g provides 152×126/252 = 76 g of chromic oxide
(c) 252 g of ammonium dichromate produces 22.4 l of nitrogen; 126 g produces 22.4×126/252 = 11.2 l of nitrogen
